summary.motive: Disguise a five-man fire zone behind a stacked single-high shell so spread protections commit to the wrong crosser while the safety-corner exchange manufactures interior heat.
summary.keyDefender: RCB darting inside — the blitzer whose delayed inside path arrives after the protection has fully committed to the widened safety
summary.whyItWorks: The cross scrambles counting rules, the back can only block one dog, and the fire-zone rotation has occupied every hot window before the quarterback finishes his hitch.
summary.failureMode: Hot throws released on rhythm before the cross develops — if the ball is out early, only three linemen rushed and the vacated zones are still empty.

beats.title: 1. The Stacked Disguise
beats.text: Single-high shell, three backers stacked directly behind three linemen, corners playing soft — it reads like plain Cover 3. Nothing in the picture announces that two defensive backs are about to rush.

beats.title: 2. Safety and Corner Begin the Cross
beats.text: The walked safety widens his rush lane toward the edge while the corner darts inside off it. Their paths swap mid-rush — whoever the protection assigns to each will be blocking the wrong man.

beats.title: 3. Fire Zone Floods Behind
beats.text: Three deep thirds rotate behind three under-zone droppers, and every quick window fills before the quarterback finishes his hitch. The drag hits Mike’s wall, the checkdown dies in Sam’s flat.

beats.title: 4. Hot Window Belongs to the Hook
beats.text: The running back slides to the darting corner, leaving the widened safety unblocked — so the hot throw comes out early, directly into Will’s flooding hook zone. Tipped at the catch point.

relations.tell: Pre-snap it reads single-high Cover 3 with stacked backers — the tell is only the safety creeping to nine yards without any linebacker moving with him.
